qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? I started at age 19 at a local jiu-jitsu gym after two years of training wrestling in high school. I wanted to continue doing something competitive, and a year later I started striking and blending it together.

Training: Run 4 miles when I wake up. Then I have MMA drilling or strength and conditioning in the afternoon. I teach kids’ jiu-jitsu, then I have MMA drilling and five rounds of technical sparring or live goes from various positions. 

What ranks and titles have you held? Brown belt in jiu-jitsu, Team wrestling State Champs, three-time All-American in wrestling. XFN 125-lb champ.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? I've been given a great opportunity and all my sacrifices and hard work are paying off. It means I can make a better life for my daughter.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I'm in the process of getting a kinesiology degree but I've taken a few semesters off since The Ultimate Fighter and now being in the UFC. I don't take this opportunity lightly and I want to give the UFC 100% of my focus at this time.

What was your job before you started fighting? I started fighting basically straight out of high school. I was a full-time mom and college student while training.

Favorite grappling technique: D’Arce choke

Favorite Striking technique: High Jab

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started more than eight years ago with jiu-jitsu, and from my first class, I fell in love with this discipline. I began to compete a lot in jiu-jitsu and I got completely into the world of martial arts. I saw the UFC and I told my coach that I wanted to fight. We started training all the other elements of MMA until they gave me the opportunity to have my first fight as an amateur, and going up to the cage was the best feeling of my life. From there, my dream was to reach the UFC. I trained and visualized myself every day fighting there, and now I will fulfill my dream that I worked so hard for. Many people did not believe that I would make it, but I always promised my son Matias that I would. I promised him that I will make it to the UFC and my coach always believed in me.

What ranks and titles have you held? I am a 12-time national champion of jiu-jitsu, absolute champion of the most important jiu-jitsu tournaments in the country, I was undefeated as an amateur and I am undefeated as a professional doing all my professional career outside of Mexico in the United States.

Do you have any heroes? My son Matias is my hero, he always has the best attitude before any situation.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? This question touches my heart; it means EVERYTHING. Since I started fighting, I wake up every day thinking I wanted to be there. I trained thinking that one day I would be there. My coach, every time we were in camp, told me we are not preparing for this fight, we are preparing for when we get to the UFC. People around us saw it as impossible and they thought we were crazy. Although we did not have the absolute certainty that we would achieve it all the time, we woke up, dreamed and trained for that. The discipline and love for what I do paid off and I fell asleep many times thinking that I wanted to someday be there listening as they introduced me. Fighting in that cage is the best thing that has happened to me and is a dream and an achievement for this part of Mexico. For my first fight in the UFC, I talked to all my family, including my grandmother Amparo, and she was very excited to see me finally fight there, and unfortunately, she passed away a few days later, on July 27. She could not see me fight there and fulfill my dream, so apart from dedicating all the fights to my son Matias, this fight goes to my grandmother in heaven that would have loved to see me there for the first time.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I have a degree in international tourism.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? Undefeated at 4-0

Ranks in any martial arts styles: BJJ purple belt

Favorite grappling technique: Armbar and kimura

Favorite Striking technique: My cross and hook

Training: We are doing 4 a days every day. Training like this is a championship fight.



When and why did you start training for fighting? I started martial arts at age 8 and I have always had a passion for combat sports.



What ranks and titles have you held? ICF 155lbs Champion, Shidokan World Champion, Shidokan U.S. Champion, ISCF regional grappling champion, GA Games boxing champion



Do you have any heroes? Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)



What is your favorite technique? Anything that finishes the fight



What does it mean for you to fight in the WEC? It’s a great opportunity to showcase my talents for the MMA fans on a premier platform (WEC)



Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Yes, a degree in Public Health


What was your job before you started fighting? College Student


Most memorable professional fight (who, where, why)? My first fight versus Cam McHargue. He was 9-1 and I was an underdog, I won the fight by TKO. It was good to beat the odds.



What was your most challenging professional fight (against who, when, what was the outcome)? Nick Diaz was my most challenging fight. We were contracted to fight at 160 lbs. At the weigh ins I weighed 158 lbs, I was informed that Nick could not make weight. We ended up fighting at welterweight. It was a good fight, but I came up short. Nick is a great competitor and I would love to fight him at 155 or 160 instead of 170.



Did you compete in any other sport(s) at college or professional level? Yes, I competed in amateur and professional boxing and Muay Thai



Who were your training partners for this fight? All the guys at team Lloyd Irvin and I'm working a lot with 10-0 prospect Stephen Bass and former 2 division boxing champion Norman Jones.



Did you put more emphasis towards a fighting style or adjust your training to prepare for your opponent? We always have a gameplan and I have an amazing team helping me prepare. We are making sure that I am strong at every range and in super good shape. I feel like I'm in shape to go 5 rounds now.



What other than WINNING, are you using for motivation for the fight? I not only want to win but I want to get a bonus (submission, KO or fight of the night). I want to travel to do some humanitarian work and I want that bonus to fund it. So I'm using violence to pay for me to do some positive things in the world. Also, I have to prove that I belong in the cage with the best. I ran into some bad luck in my last fight and need to show that that fight was a fluke.



What is your favorite thing about this sport? The training/ grind. Pushing yourself to your limits and beyond.



How long do you see yourself staying in this sport? I want to be the best 155 lbs fighter in the World.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I’ve been training since a young age. I was always running the mountains, and since a young age I was getting prepared. I started training for fighting in 2017. 

What ranks and titles have you held? Kyrgyz MMA champion, Bator FC Grand Prix champion

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means everything for me to fight in the UFC. This is my moment, and this is all I’ve been training and preparing for my whole life. When a dream becomes a plan, it happens. 

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career? My debut in the UFC was the most important fight in my career, I step on 4 days short notice. I didn’t want to lose, my whole country was watching me, I was the first fully blooded Kyrgyz fighter in the UFC and this win was the most important for me.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? To show the right path for the younger generation, fighting is not the most important. The way you carry yourself is the most important

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I have a law degree from Kyrgyzstan University. 

What was your job before you started fighting? I never had a job. 

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I am a former amateur world champion in MMA

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: I love horses, I love to play KokBuru. I love reading books

What is one thing you want UFC fans to know about you? I’m a mountain humble fighter, I came across the world to America, just to be in the UFC. UFC changed my life and gave me a dream that I’ve been chasing for a long time. Everything is possible. When I started my career my coach and me had the same vision. To be in the UFC, and god gave me this opportunity.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? I am finally able to showcase my skillset on the world stage where I belong.
Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I finished high school and then began working and training. I didn't pursue further education.
What was your job before you started fighting? I worked for DHL Pharmacy Supply - the job entailed organizing ordered drugs and supplies to be distributed to hospitals and pharmacies Australia-wide.
Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? Rd 2 armbar victory - 1-0 as an amateur

Favorite Striking technique: Right hook

TRAINING: In the morning I go to a training session (private lesson). After that I go to work. After work, it’s training again! In the evening at 9pm I come home, eat something and at 22.30 I go to bed.

When and why did you start training for fighting? When I was 10 years old I started with taekwondo. At the age of 14 I got a black belt and at the age of 16 I got the 2nd dan. When I was 18 years old I stopped taekwondo because the school closed. Then I started with weightlifting. In 2001, me and my friend and teammate Gerald Turek found the first UFC DVDs in a shop. After that, we searched for an MMA club in Vienna because we were very fascinated with the sport. In 2002 we found the first MMA school in Vienna and we started MMA.

What ranks and titles have you held? 2nd dan black belt in taekwondo, Austrian MMA champion, WFC heavyweight champion

Do you have any heroes? Jean Claude Van Damme or Steven Seagal - he he joke! ;) Fedor Emelianenko is my biggest heavyweight legend, Junior dos Santos, Cain Velasquez and Alistar Overeem are now my absolute heroes!

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It’s a big honor and pleasure to get the opportunity to fight in the UFC. To fight in the UFC is the goal and the dream for every fighter like me.

What was your job before you started fighting? I work as a bodyguard until now!

Favorite Striking technique: Punches with kicks
